summary: Nora's @-mentions on Instagram now actually ping the person, instead of going out as plain text with no notification.
details: Measured live, 2026-09-22: Nora sent "@Miles Novak ..." with the mention correctly addressed to the right account, and it rendered as an ordinary sentence -- no ping, nothing in any log to say it had failed. Instagram only turns a mention into a ping when the message text at that exact spot reads "@" plus the account's own username; Nora writes a mention the way she writes any name -- the one she knows the person by ("Miles Novak") -- so the text never matched what Instagram was looking for, even though every other part of the mention (which account, which word) was already correct.

identity.toml can now carry that username next to a person's Instagram account (it was already an accepted field, just never read by anything). When it is present, nora/platform/instagram/send.py rewrites the mention's own span in the outbound text to "@<username>" right before the message leaves for the Instagram bridge, and recomputes the position of every other mention in the same message so a second @-mention after it still points at the right words. The record Nora keeps of what she said is unaffected -- it still reads the name she meant, not the raw handle.

The username is authored by the operator per account, not read live off Instagram's own member list. That was a deliberate choice: the alternative (pulling it from the room's roster each time) is self-updating but changes a lookup shared by four platforms for one platform's need; a per-account field costs nothing else and an operator who renames an account just re-types one line.

nora/persons.py exposes it as Persons.instagram_handle(fbid) -- looked up by the exact account (fbid) a mention resolved to, not by person, since one person can hold more than one Instagram account with different handles.
limitations: Until an operator adds `username = "..."` beside an account's `fbid` in identity.toml, an Instagram mention still goes out as plain text with no ping -- unchanged from before this fix, and never an error.
A renamed Instagram handle goes stale until the operator updates identity.toml by hand; nothing here notices a rename on its own.

Whether Instagram's own mention API wants the offset/length in UTF-16 code units or something else remains unmeasured -- no probe against a live account was run for this fix (the repo's working rules forbid it), and this was already true, unmeasured, before this change of every mention Nora has ever sent on this platform.
